investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past agent creation.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 are ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch, leaving only 2 nodes that can schedule remote-agent pods. At the time of the eval run, both of those nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and preemption found no victims, so all three probe pods remained unschedulable for 140–147 seconds before the checks timed out and failed. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/un-cleaned VMs from prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets a label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to nodes that are already at capacity.

Tertiary — VM resource leak from a prior eval run: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is responsible for releasing resources; if a previous run's cleanup failed, VM slots may remain occupied and unavailable to new pods.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may not have enough VM quota to handle concurrent observability probes plus any live workload running at the same time.

investigation.title: Remote Agents: All Three Checks Failing Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity on Kubernetes Cluster
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents observability evals (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-18T05:05–05:10Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message: 0/6 nodes are available, 2 nodes reporting Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm and 4 nodes not matching the pod's node affinity/selector. The eval probe could not schedule a remote agent pod, so the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and the expected-output contract fully unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. Because no preemption victims exist and preemption is not helpful, the scheduler cannot place the pod at all. The eval probe times out waiting for the pod to become schedulable, the agent is never created, and no evidence is written — causing the remote-agent-state check (and its siblings) to fail with a complete contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

source-context.infra/evals/status/check-expectations.json:255-263: the remote-agent-state contract at line 261 requires orgId, agentId, readyState, state — none of which can be populated if the pod never schedules.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: all available VM slots are consumed by existing pods, leaving no capacity for new remote agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity/selector mismatch on the remaining 4 nodes: those nodes are not labeled or tainted to accept remote agent pods, so even if VM capacity existed elsewhere it would not be usable without affinity changes.

Tertiary — cluster has not scaled out to add additional kata peer-pods capable nodes: the cluster has exactly 6 nodes and no autoscaler or preemption policy is able to free capacity in time for the eval timeout.

Lower probability — a recent deployment or workload spike consumed the remaining VM slots just before the eval window at 05:05Z, causing a transient exhaustion rather than a permanent capacity ceiling.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Prevents Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because the Kubernetes scheduler could not place the required kata peer-pod VM onto any of the 6 available nodes — 2 nodes reported insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never became schedulable, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, no evidence was collected, and the expected-output contract for remote-agent-runtime (requiring orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) was entirely unmet.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature in production-api has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource on the 2 nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector. The scheduler message "0/6 nodes are available: 2 Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm, 4 node(s) didn't match Pod's node affinity/selector" (evidence: failed-check.message, sibling.remote-agent-create, sibling.remote-agent-state) confirms that no schedulable capacity exists for new remote agent pods. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion condition, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct consequence: the probe in run-status-probes.mjs calls createAgent with type "remote" (source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1789-1797), which requires a kata peer-pod VM to be provisioned, and that provisioning is blocked at the scheduler level before any agent runtime logic executes.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhaustion on the 2 affinity-matching nodes: existing remote agent pods or other workloads have consumed all available VM slots on the nodes that satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector, leaving zero capacity for new eval pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's affinity/selector, reducing the schedulable pool to only 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes have reduced capacity (e.g., due to node scaling events, maintenance, or resource reclamation lag), exhaustion is more likely.

Tertiary — kata peer-pod provider quota or upstream VM pool limit: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource may be backed by an external VM pool (e.g., cloud provider quota) that is at capacity, preventing the node-level resource from being replenished even if pods are deleted.

Lower probability — node affinity/selector on the eval pod is overly restrictive and does not match nodes with available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, creating a scheduling deadlock even if capacity exists elsewhere in the cluster.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was left unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was collected because the pod never reached a running state, so the eval runner could not advance past agent creation.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry it. Of the 6 total nodes, 4 are ineligible due to node affinity or selector mismatch, leaving only 2 nodes that can schedule remote-agent pods. At the time of the eval run, both of those nodes reported "Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm" and preemption found no victims, so all three probe pods remained unschedulable for 140–147 seconds before the checks timed out and failed. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity constraint; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 eligible nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/un-cleaned VMs from prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new probe pods.

Secondary — node affinity or selector misconfiguration: the pod spec targets a label or taint that only 2 of 6 nodes satisfy, artificially constraining the schedulable pool to nodes that are already at capacity.

Tertiary — VM resource leak from a prior eval run: the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is responsible for releasing resources; if a previous run's cleanup failed, VM slots may remain occupied and unavailable to new pods.

Quaternary — cluster under-provisioning: the 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes may not have enough VM quota to handle concurrent observability probes plus any live workload running at the same time.

The eval probe could not schedule a remote agent pod, so the createAgent call in run-status-probes.mjs never completed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) unpopulated and the expected-output contract fully unmet.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agents feature has exhausted its allocatable kata.peerpods.io/vm resource across the 2 nodes that carry that resource type. The remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector requirements. Because no preemption victims exist and preemption is not helpful, the scheduler cannot place the pod at all. The eval probe times out waiting for the pod to become schedulable, the agent is never created, and no evidence is written — causing the remote-agent-state check (and its siblings) to fail with a complete contract gap. This is an eval-observed infrastructure capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pods VM resource pool; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence.
